title: Fe²⁺ homogeneous catalysis of I⁻ / S₂O₈²⁻
observation: Fe²⁺ pale-green solution may become more yellow/brown as Fe³⁺ forms; colour change may be masked at low concentration
notes: first catalytic step; Fe²⁺ is regenerated in the next step.

title: Regeneration of Fe²⁺ in I⁻ / S₂O₈²⁻ catalysis
observation: iodine gives a yellow-brown / brown solution; with starch gives blue-black
notes: second catalytic step; catalyst is regenerated.

title: NO / NO₂ homogeneous catalysis of SO₂ oxidation
reagent: NO acts in a catalytic cycle
observation: NO is colourless; NO₂ is brown gas
notes: conceptual catalyst-cycle example.

title: NO₂ oxidises SO₂
observation: brown NO₂ is consumed; NO formed is colourless
notes: completes the atmospheric NOx catalytic cycle. ---

title: Thermal decomposition of Group 2 carbonates
observation: gas evolved; CO₂ turns limewater milky; solid remains
notes: thermal stability increases down Group 2, so more heating is required down the group.

title: Thermal decomposition of Group 2 nitrates
observation: white CuI precipitate forms together with brown iodine solution
notes: iodine may be confirmed with starch → blue-black. ---

title: Benzene chlorination
observation: chlorine colour is consumed; HCl may be evolved; no single distinctive observation is normally required
notes: electrophilic substitution.

title: Benzene bromination
observation: bromine colour is consumed; no white precipitate
notes: **do not confuse with phenol/phenylamine**, which react with Br₂(aq) without AlBr₃.

title: Benzene nitration
observation: no distinctive required colour change; nitrobenzene is a pale-yellow oily liquid in practice
notes: exact 25–60 °C range is worth memorising.

title: Friedel–Crafts alkylation
notes: electrophilic substitution.

title: Friedel–Crafts acylation
notes: electrophilic substitution.

title: Complete oxidation of alkylbenzene side-chain
reactants: alkylbenzene with at least one benzylic H, e.g. methylbenzene
reagent: hot alkaline KMnO₄, then dilute acid
observation: purple KMnO₄ is decolourised / reduced; after acidification benzoic acid may crystallise as a white solid
notes: any oxidisable alkyl side-chain is converted to `–COOH`.

title: Hydrogenation of benzene ring
notes: ring addition, not electrophilic substitution.

title: Methylbenzene side-chain halogenation
temperature: light / mild heating may be used
notes: conditions determine **side-chain** substitution; `AlCl₃/AlBr₃` instead promotes **ring** substitution. ---

title: Formation of chlorobenzene / bromobenzene
reagent: AlCl₃ for chlorination / AlBr₃ for bromination
notes: same chemistry as A2-30-01/02; listed again because Topic 31 explicitly requires the preparation route.

title: Halogenoarene resistance to ordinary nucleophilic substitution
reagent: e.g. NaOH(aq) under ordinary halogenoalkane conditions
products: essentially no reaction under conditions that readily hydrolyse chloroalkanes
notes: C–Cl bond has partial double-bond character from delocalisation; C atom is sp². ---

title: Alcohol acylation
observation: reaction occurs readily; steamy/acidic HCl fumes may be seen
notes: no concentrated H₂SO₄ catalyst is required. ---

title: Phenol + NaOH
observation: phenol dissolves more readily as soluble sodium phenoxide forms; no gas
notes: distinguishes phenol from ordinary alcohols.

title: Phenol + sodium metal
observation: effervescence; sodium disappears; H₂ gives a squeaky pop
notes: acid–metal reaction.

title: Phenol nitration
observation: no single CIE-mandated colour observation; nitrated products form readily
notes: compare with benzene: phenol does **not** require conc. HNO₃/conc. H₂SO₄.

title: Phenol bromination
observation: bromine water decolourises and a **white precipitate** forms
notes: no AlBr₃ catalyst.

title: Phenol + diazonium salt (azo coupling)
reagent: diazonium salt in the presence of NaOH(aq)
observation: intensely coloured azo dye forms, commonly orange/red/yellow depending on structure
notes: coupling occurs mainly at the 4-position if free. ---

title: Alkylbenzene → benzoic acid
reagent: hot alkaline KMnO₄, then dilute acid
observation: purple permanganate decolourises; white benzoic-acid crystals may form after acidification/cooling
notes: duplicate of A2-30-06 because Topic 33 explicitly requires it. ---

title: Carboxylic acid + PCl₃
section: 33B. Conversion of carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides
observation: corrosive reaction; no single standard CIE observation required
notes: syllabus explicitly associates **PCl₃ with heat**.

title: Carboxylic acid + PCl₅
section: 33B. Conversion of carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides
observation: steamy/acidic HCl fumes may be observed
notes: useful qualitative conversion route.

title: Carboxylic acid + SOCl₂
section: 33B. Conversion of carboxylic acids to acyl chlorides
observation: gas evolution; steamy acidic HCl fumes; SO₂ also evolved
notes: gaseous by-products help drive reaction forward. ---

title: Methanoic acid + Fehling's reagent
products: CO₂ + H₂O + Cu₂O(s) from reduction of Cu²⁺
notes: methanoic acid behaves as a reducing agent.

title: Methanoic acid + Tollens' reagent
notes: methanoic acid is an exception among ordinary carboxylic acids.

title: Methanoic acid + acidified KMnO₄
observation: purple → colourless; CO₂ may be evolved
notes: oxidation to carbon dioxide.

title: Methanoic acid + acidified K₂Cr₂O₇
observation: orange → green; CO₂ may be evolved
notes: oxidation to carbon dioxide. ---

title: Ethanedioic acid + warm acidified KMnO₄
observation: purple solution decolourises; effervescence of CO₂
notes: slow at first when cold; becomes faster as Mn²⁺ builds up. ---

title: Acyl chloride hydrolysis
observation: rapid/vigorous reaction; steamy acidic HCl fumes may be observed
notes: much more readily hydrolysed than chloroalkanes or chlorobenzene.

title: Acyl chloride + alcohol
observation: reaction occurs readily; HCl fumes may be seen
notes: ester formation; no concentrated H₂SO₄ catalyst needed.

title: Acyl chloride + phenol
medium: non-aqueous / weakly basic trapping conditions may be used experimentally
observation: ester forms; HCl may be evolved
notes: e.g. benzoyl chloride + phenol → phenyl benzoate.

title: Acyl chloride + NH₃
products: primary amide; HCl is neutralised by excess NH₃ to NH₄Cl
observation: rapid reaction; white ammonium salt / fumes may occur depending on setup
notes: net practical equation often written `RCOCl + 2NH₃ → RCONH₂ + NH₄Cl`.

title: Acyl chloride + primary amine
observation: rapid reaction; amine hydrochloride salt may form
notes: secondary amide product.

title: Acyl chloride + secondary amine
observation: rapid reaction; ammonium salt may form
notes: tertiary amide product. ---

title: Halogenoalkane + ammonia → primary amine
reagent: NH₃ in ethanol, preferably excess NH₃
products: primary amine, with ammonium halide by-product
notes: **heated under pressure / sealed system**.

title: Halogenoalkane + primary amine → secondary amine
notes: heat in a **sealed tube / under pressure**.

title: Amide reduction with LiAlH₄
notes: C=O group is reduced to CH₂.

title: Nitrile reduction with LiAlH₄
notes: carbon chain is retained; nitrile carbon becomes CH₂.

title: Nitrile hydrogenation
notes: an alternative to LiAlH₄. ---

title: Nitrobenzene reduction to phenylamine
medium: strongly acidic reduction, then alkaline work-up
observation: tin dissolves during reduction; no single final colour observation is required
notes: NaOH liberates free phenylamine from the phenylammonium salt.

title: Phenylamine + bromine water
observation: bromine water decolourises and a **white precipitate** forms
notes: activated aromatic ring; no AlBr₃ catalyst.

title: Diazotisation of phenylamine
observation: usually a clear diazonium solution; no dramatic visible change is required
notes: **temperature must stay below 10 °C** because the diazonium salt decomposes on warming.

title: Diazonium salt hydrolysis to phenol
notes: direct conversion phenylamine → diazonium → phenol.

title: Diazonium coupling with phenol
notes: azo linkage is `–N=N–`.

title: Amine protonation
observation: amine often becomes more water-soluble; no characteristic colour change
notes: acid–base behaviour used when comparing basicities. ---

title: Amide acid hydrolysis
notes: for `RCONH₂`, nitrogen product is NH₄⁺ under acidic conditions.

title: Amide alkaline hydrolysis
observation: ammonia may be evolved from primary amides; NH₃ turns damp red litmus blue
notes: acidification afterwards gives the free carboxylic acid.

title: Amide reduction
notes: same transformation as A2-34-03. ---

title: Amino acid + acid
notes: basis of electrophoresis behaviour at low pH.

title: Amino acid + base
notes: basis of electrophoresis behaviour at high pH.

title: Peptide-bond formation
notes: forms `–CONH–` peptide linkage. ---

title: Polyester from diol + dicarboxylic acid
observation: viscous polymer forms; water is eliminated
notes: exact laboratory apparatus/temperature is not normally memorised.

title: Polyester from diol + dioyl chloride
reagent: monomers themselves; base may be used to remove HCl
observation: polymer may form rapidly at interface
notes: acyl chlorides are more reactive than dicarboxylic acids.

title: Polyester from hydroxycarboxylic acid
observation: polymer formation; no distinctive colour change
notes: one monomer contains both functional groups.

title: Polyamide from diamine + dicarboxylic acid
notes: amide links `–CONH–`.

title: Polyamide from diamine + dioyl chloride
observation: polymer fibre/film can form at the interface ("nylon-rope" style experiment)
notes: laboratory-reproducible demonstration.

title: Polyamide / polypeptide from aminocarboxylic acid or amino acid
notes: conceptual syllabus reaction.

title: Polyester acid hydrolysis
notes: basis of biodegradability of condensation polymers.

title: Polyester alkaline hydrolysis
notes: saponification-type cleavage.

title: Polyamide acid hydrolysis
notes: peptide bonds are hydrolysed similarly.

title: Polyamide alkaline hydrolysis
notes: hydrolyses amide links. --- > These are not all "A2-only", but they are printed in the current 9701 practical qualitative-analysis notes and are useful for any laboratory simulator.

title: Al³⁺ + NaOH
products: Al(OH)₃(s), then soluble aluminate complex in excess OH⁻
notes: amphoteric behaviour.

title: Al³⁺ + NH₃
notes: distinguishes from Zn²⁺.

title: NH₄⁺ + NaOH
observation: ammonia evolved; damp red litmus turns blue
notes: standard ammonium test.

title: Ba²⁺ + NaOH
products: slight Ba(OH)₂ / precipitate only if concentration permits
observation: faint white ppt unless `[Ba²⁺]` is very low
notes: NH₃ gives no ppt.

title: Ca²⁺ + NaOH
observation: white ppt unless `[Ca²⁺]` is very low
notes: NH₃ gives no ppt.

title: Cr³⁺ + NaOH
observation: grey-green ppt; **soluble in excess giving dark-green solution**
notes: highly characteristic.

title: Cu²⁺ + NH₃
observation: pale-blue ppt → dissolves in excess to give **dark-blue solution**

title: Fe²⁺ + NaOH
products: Fe(OH)₂(s), then oxidation products on standing in air
observation: **green ppt turning brown on contact with air**; insoluble in excess
notes: air oxidation is an important observation.

title: Fe²⁺ + NH₃
observation: green ppt turning brown in air; insoluble in excess

title: Mn²⁺ + NaOH
products: Mn(OH)₂(s), then oxidised manganese species in air
observation: **off-white ppt rapidly turning brown on contact with air**; insoluble in excess

title: Mn²⁺ + NH₃
observation: off-white ppt rapidly turning brown in air; insoluble in excess

title: Zn²⁺ + NH₃
notes: key distinction from Al³⁺. ---

title: Bromide + Ag⁺
observation: **cream / off-white ppt**, partially soluble in NH₃(aq)

title: Nitrate + Al / OH⁻
observation: NH₃ evolved; damp red litmus turns blue
notes: nitrite gives the same ammonia result, so another test may be needed.

title: Nitrite + acidified KMnO₄
notes: distinguishes from nitrate.

title: Sulfate + Ba²⁺
observation: **white ppt**, insoluble in excess dilute strong acids
notes: high `[Ca²⁺]` can also give white CaSO₄ ppt.

title: Sulfite + Ba²⁺ then acid
observation: white ppt forms then **dissolves in dilute strong acid**
notes: sulfite also decolourises acidified KMnO₄.

title: Thiosulfate + acid
observation: **off-white / pale-yellow precipitate slowly forms**; mixture becomes cloudy
notes: sulfur precipitate can obscure a mark beneath the flask in rate experiments. ---

title: CO₂ test
notes: excess CO₂ can redissolve precipitate by forming soluble hydrogencarbonate, though not required for the basic test.

title: I₂ + starch
notes: very sensitive iodine test. ---

title: Aldehyde + Fehling's reagent
section: Part III — Organic functional-group tests that can appear in practical work
notes: ketones generally negative.

title: Aldehyde + Tollens' reagent
section: Part III — Organic functional-group tests that can appear in practical work
notes: ketones generally negative.

title: Iodoform / triiodomethane test
section: Part III — Organic functional-group tests that can appear in practical work
notes: classic methyl ketone / suitable secondary alcohol test.

title: Acidified KMnO₄ oxidation test
section: Part III — Organic functional-group tests that can appear in practical work
notes: not specific to one functional group.

title: Carbonyl + 2,4-DNPH
section: Part III — Organic functional-group tests that can appear in practical work
notes: detects C=O in aldehydes and ketones. --- > Paper 4 explicitly assumes AS knowledge. These are the high-value "carry-over" transformations that often connect A2 synthesis pathways.

title: Alkane free-radical halogenation
notes: substitution; often gives mixture.

title: Alkene + Br₂(aq)
notes: test for C=C.

title: Alkene + H₂
notes: hydrogenation.

title: Alkene + steam
notes: electrophilic addition.

title: Alkene + HX
notes: Markovnikov outcome may matter for unsymmetrical alkenes.

title: Alkene + cold dilute acidified KMnO₄
notes: oxidation without C=C cleavage.

title: Alkene oxidative cleavage
products: carbonyl compounds / carboxylic acids / CO₂ depending on substitution
notes: used to locate C=C positions. ---

title: Halogenoalkane → alcohol
notes: nucleophilic substitution.

title: Halogenoalkane → nitrile
notes: carbon chain length increases by one carbon.

title: Halogenoalkane → amine
notes: **heated under pressure**; excess NH₃ favours primary amine.

title: Halogenoalkane elimination
notes: contrast `NaOH(aq)` substitution vs `NaOH in ethanol` elimination.

title: Halogenoalkane + ethanolic AgNO₃
observation: AgCl white / AgBr cream / AgI pale yellow precipitate
notes: rate indicates relative C–X bond reactivity. ---

title: Primary alcohol → aldehyde
observation: dichromate orange → green / permanganate purple → colourless
notes: **distil product as it forms** to prevent further oxidation.

title: Primary alcohol → carboxylic acid
reagent: excess acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ or acidified KMnO₄
notes: **reflux**.

title: Secondary alcohol → ketone
notes: distillation commonly used.

title: Alcohol dehydration
reagent: conc. H₂SO₄ or heated Al₂O₃ catalyst
notes: elimination.

title: Fischer esterification
observation: often fruity ester smell, but odour should not be relied on as an exam observation unless instructed
notes: reversible equilibrium. ---

title: Aldehyde / ketone reduction
medium: NaBH₄ often aqueous/alcoholic; LiAlH₄ dry ether
products: primary alcohol from aldehyde / secondary alcohol from ketone
notes: nucleophilic reduction.

title: Carbonyl + HCN
notes: nucleophilic addition; introduces one extra carbon. ---

title: Nitrile acid hydrolysis
notes: carbon chain retained.

title: Nitrile alkaline hydrolysis
reagent: dilute NaOH(aq), then acidify if free acid required

title: Ester acid hydrolysis
notes: reversible.

title: Ester alkaline hydrolysis
notes: effectively irreversible under normal conditions.

title: Carboxylic acid + carbonate
notes: distinguishes carboxylic acid from phenol/alcohol.

title: Carboxylic acid reduction
notes: strong reducing agent required. --- 1. **Benzene + Br₂:** `Br₂ + AlBr₃`, no bromine water test conditions. 2. **Phenol + Br₂(aq):** RT, no catalyst → bromine water decolourises + **white ppt**. 3. **Phenylamine + Br₂(aq):** RT, no catalyst → bromine water decolourises + **white ppt**. 4. **Benzene nitration:** conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄, **25–60 °C**. 5. **Phenol nitration:** **dilute HNO₃(aq), RT**. 6. **Diazotisation:** `NaNO₂ + dilute acid`, **below 10 °C**. 7. **Diazonium → phenol:** **warm with water**, N₂ effervescence. 8. **Alkylbenzene → benzoic acid:** **hot alkaline KMnO₄, then dilute acid**. 9. **Acyl chloride reactions:** generally **RT**; no Fischer esterification catalyst required. 10. **RX → alcohol:** `NaOH(aq) + heat`. 11. **RX → alkene:** `NaOH in ethanol + heat`. 12. **RX → nitrile:** `KCN in ethanol + heat`. 13. **RX → amine:** `NH₃ in ethanol + heat under pressure`. 14. **Primary alcohol → aldehyde:** oxidise and **distil**. 15. **Primary alcohol → acid:** oxidise under **reflux**. 16. **Methanoic acid:** positive Tollens / Fehling and decolourises acidified KMnO₄. 17. **Ethanedioic acid + KMnO₄:** must be **warm and acidic**. 18. **Cu²⁺ + excess NH₃:** deep-blue solution. 19. **Co²⁺ + excess Cl⁻:** pink → blue. 20. **Cu²⁺ + I⁻:** white CuI ppt + brown iodine. --- For implementation, each record can map directly to: ```text id topic priority reactants[] reagent[] temperature medium products[] observation[] notes[] ``` For simulation logic, separate: - `required_conditions` - `catalyst` - `solvent_or_medium` - `temperature_range` - `visible_colour_before` - `visible_colour_after` - `precipitate_colour` - `gas_evolved` - `reversible` - `reaction_type` - `exam_priority` This prevents a single free-text `observation` field from becoming hard to query later. --- - Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry 9701 syllabus, examinations 2025–2027. - A Level Topics 23–37, especially Topics 26–36. - Current Cambridge qualitative-analysis notes used for 9701 practical assessment. - Paper 4 syllabus statement: A Level questions are based on A Level content, but knowledge of AS content is required.
